issues.description: The problem statement and template expect an interface named 'Milkable' with method messageOnMilk(), but the solution repository introduces an interface named 'Dairy' (and leaves Milkable.java empty). Classes in the solution (Goat, Seal) implement 'Dairy' instead of 'Milkable', which is a structural/type-name mismatch that would confuse students about the correct interface name and contract to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name across artifacts. Rename the solution's 'Dairy' interface to 'Milkable' (or ensure 'Milkable' is properly implemented) and update Goat and Seal to implement 'Milkable'. Remove or repurpose the empty Milkable.java in the solution so the interface name matches the problem statement and the template contract.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to an interface named 'Milkable' (the UML and Main.java use Milkable), but the solution implementation introduced an interface named 'Dairy' which Goat and Seal implement. This is a conflicting identifier for the same conceptual entity (animals that can be milked) and will confuse students mapping the requirements to the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent interface name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's 'Dairy' interface to 'Milkable' (and update Goat and Seal to implement Milkable), or alternatively rename all references of 'Milkable' in the problem and template to 'Dairy' so the interface identifier is identical in problem, template, and solution.
